idiom_name: kotlin-logging KLogger plus a chained javax.crypto.Mac writer
implementation_notes: Kotlin has no logging facility of its own, so the idiom is the JVM pair: a Kotlin facade such as kotlin-logging (which wraps SLF4J) supplies the chokepoint, and javax.crypto.Mac with a prepared HmacSHA256 instance produces the chained tag. Keep the chain in one injected component rather than in a top-level logger, and define a canonical form instead of relying on data-class toString(); the hand-written appender is justified when the audit stream must not share the application logger's configuration or rotation.
pitfalls: KotlinLogging.logger {} builds a logger per call site; the chain must live in a single object (injected singleton, not a logger factory) or every call site gets its own chain head.
By-name logging arguments are evaluated on the logging thread at an arbitrary later time - build and store the canonical record first, and never let a lambda close over mutable state.
Kotlin/JVM will happily log a data class whose toString() prints a token or an email address; define an explicit redacting canonical form for audit events instead.
